entityName: UNIV FIRENZE - Centro per la Protezione Civile dell'Università di Firenze (CPC)
entityDescription:
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence (CPC-UNIFI) has been constituted in 2018 within the University of Florence in accordance with the article 36 of the Statute of the University of Florence (Italy) and of the University Regulations on Service Centers. 
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence is part of the National Italian Service of Civil Protection, as it is Centre of Competence for Civil Protection in the field of geological risk prevention. The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence is currently composed of about 20 staff people (technicians, administrators, researchers, professors) and several temporary positions (research assistants, research fellows and visiting scientists).
The personnel of CPC-UNIFI is enrolled to the Earth Sciences Department of the University of Florence, one of the largest centres in geological sciences in Italy. The Earth Sciences Department has been recognised since 2005 as national Centre of Competence for Civil Protection in the field of geological risk prevention, until the establishment of CPC-UNIFI. The Italian legislation (Decree of the Italian Prime Minister of 27 February 2004; Decree of the Head of the National Civil Protection Department no. 252 of 25 January 2005, Decree of the Head of the National Civil Protection Department no. 3152 of 24 July 2013) entrusts it with the aims of technological and scientific support for safeguarding the integrity of life, goods, buildings and environment from any damage or risk of damage arising from natural and anthropic disasters. 
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence provides technical and research support to all the University's Civil Protection structures, management of emergencies, prevention and reduction of natural and anthropic hazards and risks. It integrates technical-scientific knowledge and the products derived from research, development and innovation activities as well as academic skills in the Civil Protection network and services in accordance with the article 1 of italian Law 30/2012.
The Civil Protection Centre of the University of Florence has a firm reputation for its research expertise and practical problem solving approach to the geohazards and risk preparedness, prevention and management, which has led to the establishment of solid ties with numerous governmental agencies, private enterprises, national and international research groups as well as with regional, provincial and municipal authorities in charge of Civil Protection and environmental management.
The CPC-UNIFI is strongly linked to the UNESCO Chair on Prevention and Sustaible Management of Geo-hydrological hazards. The UNESCO chair is member of several important international consortia such as: International Consortium on Landslides (ICL) (founding member since 2002); International Consortium on Geo-disaster Reduction (ICGdR) (since 2014); Global Alliance of Disaster Research Institutes (GADRI) (founding member since 2015) and it is signatory of the ISDR-ICL Sendai Partnership 2015-2025 for global promotion of understanding and reducing disaster risk, launched by the International Strategy for Disaster Reduction (ISDR) and by the International Consortium on Landslides (ICL).

entityDescription:
The National Institute of Research and Development in Tourism - INCDT is the only institution in Romania specialized in scientific research of national interest in the field of tourism, having a vast experience accumulated over its 49 years of continuous activity. The role of INCDT is to substantiate the scientific basis for the development of Romanian tourism, to contribute to increasing the competitiveness of this sector, and to develop national and local strategies in this field.
INCDT has a close cooperation with the Ministry of Tourism, with the Ministry of Regional Development and Public Administration and Ministry of European Funds, as well as with other national and international tourism organizations. Also, INCDT is part of certain associations (European Cultural Tourism Network), clusters specialized in spa and health tourism (Innovative Cluster “Health Factory” - founding member, Regional Balneoturistic Cluster, North-West Transilvania), working groups (Ecotourism Label for Destinations - EU Ecolabel Label - established by the Ministry of Tourism), committees (Commission for Designation of Ecotourism Destinations in Romania, Inter-Institutional Commission for Assessing the Potential of Territorial Tourism, Commission of Evaluation of Tourism Investment Projects of the Ministry of Tourism), thus contributing to the development of the tourism sector through the expertise provided to them.
Our portfolio includes many types of projects (addressed both to public beneficiaries or private ones), as follows: strategies for both national and regional tourism development, as well as strategies targeting tourist destinations, including strategies by various forms of tourism; market studies, business and re-positioning /positioning studies; studies of assessment and exploitation of the natural and cultural potential of tourism and tourist product development; marketing research and strategies; documentations for the certification of localities as tourist destinations, spa resorts, or climatic resorts; databases used in the field of tourism; Tourism expertise for the development of ITC applications for the development and promotion of tourism products, pre-feasibility studies, feasibility studies etc.

The Gran Sasso Science Institute (GSSI) is an international PhD school and a center for research and higher education in the areas of Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science and Social Sciences.
As a project supported by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the GSSI has been instituted as a new Italian graduate school of advanced studies in 2016, after a three-years succesful experimental period. Located in central Italy, the school welcomes professors, researchers and students selected internationally following the best graduate schools standards worldwide. The PhD program is organized in the scientific areas of Astroparticle Physics, Mathematics, Computer science, Regional Sciences and Economic Geography. Every year we offer Post doctoral grants and research opportunities thus facilitating the attraction of high-level resources in the fields of natural and social sciences.
Through a day-to-day collaboration and interaction, researchers and students have the opportunity to build a sound knowledge of the research methods and to experiment contamination of interests, innovative approaches and multicultural exchanges in all the GSSI activities. In addressing the complexity of today’s world, we are committed to removing all barriers between the GSSI areas of study and research, where interdisciplinarity and cross-fertilization underlie everything we do. Among our goals are the dissemination of scientific results towards society and the promotion of cultural events for generic public, citizens and schools.
Our main goal is to strengthen the scientific excellence in L’Aquila area, where many skills and highly specialized structures, such as the Gran Sasso National Laboratories of the National Institute for Nuclear Physics (INFN) and the University of L'Aquila, are already present. Further, our Institute intends to promote collaborations with many national and international institutions and to interact with public and private realities in order to stimulate innovation and knowledge based communities.

Everbridge mission is to=: Keep people safe and businesses running. Faster!

We provide Software as a Server solutions for Critical Event Management

A critical event is a disruptive incident which poses serious risk or threat to assets or people. An effective Critical Event Management program and strategy is an integrated, end-to-end process that enables organizations to significantly speed up responses to critical events and improve outcomes by mitigating or eliminating the impact of a threat. Imagine your business continuity, disaster recovery, active assailant, emergency response, natural disaster, IT incident risk management, and mass notification all rolled up into an easy-to-execute, strategic plan with long-term benefits.
The four components of CEM include:

INTELLIGENCE
Proactively assess potential threats before they become critical events. With the right built-in risk intelligence and data feeds, supported by 24/7 analysts, your organization can leverage thousands of sources of data across weather, protest, social media, dark web, and hyper-local safety feeds to curate, filter and categorize risk events. This ensures a faster response to threats in order to avoid false positives and make better decisions.
CORRELATION
Align risk events to assets using a dynamic correlation engine that combines static location, expected location and last known location of people and assets. CEM can take this a step further by considering time elements to determine who or what is impacted by threats, in order to reach them faster and more decisively.
ORCHESTRATION
Automated workflows ensure that even when you and your team are not watching for threats, the system is doing it for you. SOPs, communications, and action plans can be automated and orchestrated during a crisis in order to speed up response and ensure that the appropriate action is taken for a particular threat.
ANALYTICS
With CEM, metrics are built-in throughout the process to ensure the right action is taken by the right people, at the right time, and to understand how effective actions were and how you can do better in the future.
